reference.source: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID) / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by MCOLN1 mutations affecting the endolysosomal cation channel mucolipin-1 (TRPML1), with high carrier frequency in the Ashkenazi Jewish population
Presents in infancy with delayed psychomotor development, hypotonia progressing to spasticity, and corneal clouding that may be mistaken for congenital infection or metabolic keratopathy
Progressive retinal degeneration leads to visual impairment over the first two decades, distinguishing it from static causes of infantile visual loss
A characteristic biochemical clue is constitutively elevated serum gastrin due to defective gastric parietal cell acid secretion (achlorhydria), often with a raised iron-deficiency picture
Unlike most storage disorders there is usually no organomegaly, coarse facies, or skeletal dysostosis, so it can be overlooked in the mucolipidosis/mucopolysaccharidosis differential
Diagnosis rests on MCOLN1 molecular testing supported by suggestive biochemistry; management is supportive and multidisciplinary rather than disease-modifying
reference.pathophysiology: Mucolipidosis type IV results from loss-of-function mutations in MCOLN1, encoding mucolipin-1 (TRPML1), a transient receptor potential cation channel located in late endosomes and lysosomes. Impaired channel function disrupts lysosomal calcium and iron handling, membrane trafficking, and autophagosome-lysosome fusion, so heterogeneous lipids and mucopolysaccharide-like material accumulate within enlarged storage vacuoles. Neurons, retinal cells, and gastric parietal cells are particularly vulnerable, producing the combination of neurodevelopmental impairment, retinal degeneration, corneal clouding, and achlorhydria with reactive hypergastrinaemia.
additionalDifferentials: Other lysosomal storage disorders (mucolipidosis II/III, mucopolysaccharidoses)
Congenital corneal clouding from congenital infection or metabolic keratopathy
Leukodystrophies and other causes of infantile spastic tetraparesis
Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses causing progressive visual and neurological decline
Cerebral palsy of perinatal origin (static rather than progressive)
Congenital retinal dystrophies such as Leber congenital amaurosis
additionalInvestigations: MCOLN1 gene sequencing and targeted variant testing (including common Ashkenazi founder mutations)
Serum gastrin (characteristically elevated) with gastric pH/acid studies suggesting achlorhydria
Full ophthalmological assessment with electroretinography and slit-lamp examination for corneal clouding
Brain MRI, which may show hypoplasia or dysgenesis of the corpus callosum and white-matter changes
Iron studies for associated iron-deficiency anaemia
Electron microscopy of conjunctival, skin, or other cells showing lamellar and granular storage inclusions
redFlags: Progressive rather than static loss of vision or motor skills, indicating a neurodegenerative process
Corneal clouding in an infant that mandates urgent metabolic and genetic evaluation
Unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia with markedly raised gastrin prompting achlorhydria workup
Developmental regression signalling advancing neurological disease
reference.prognosis: The disorder is slowly progressive; most affected individuals never develop speech beyond a few words and reach a developmental plateau in childhood, with visual function declining to severe impairment or blindness by early adulthood. Life expectancy can extend into adulthood with supportive care, though severe neurological disability persists.
pitfalls: Attributing early hypotonia and developmental delay to cerebral palsy and missing the progressive storage disorder
Overlooking the diagnosis because the classic storage-disease features of organomegaly and coarse facies are absent
Not recognising raised gastrin and iron-deficiency anaemia as diagnostic pointers
Delaying ophthalmological review so that treatable contributors to visual loss are not addressed
